headline: Running streak hits its longest-ever mark at 20 weeks, with aerobic efficiency visibly improving on easy efforts.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your easy-run heart rate has dropped meaningfully compared to the prior period at comparable effort — that's a concrete aerobic adaptation signal, not noise. It aligns with what you'd expect from sustained, consistent training over a long block, and it shows the base is genuinely developing rather than just accumulating kilometres.

Volume is essentially flat between the two four-week blocks, which in context is a positive. Holding near 32 km/week across 20 consecutive weeks of running — without a single dropped week — is the kind of structural consistency that builds durable fitness quietly. The 44 km long run from 25 June and the recent threshold effort at 4:24/km both confirm that the underlying capacity remains sharp; this isn't coasting volume.

Strength has been lighter these past four weeks relative to the previous block. That's worth acknowledging, not as a red flag, but as something to keep an eye on if it continues — you're carrying real strength numbers and it's worth protecting that base.
watch_items: Monitor whether the easy-run HR trend continues downward — a sustained drop from 157 to 147 is meaningful; another 2–3 runs in the same zone will confirm whether this is a real shift or block-level variance.
Keep an eye on strength session frequency over the next two weeks — four sessions in four weeks is manageable, but a second consecutive light block would start to erode the base you've built.

The lactate threshold estimate is still accumulating history; watch whether repeat efforts at similar intensities start to show pace improving for the same HR, which would corroborate the aerobic efficiency signal.
With the streak now at its personal best length, note any accumulating fatigue signals in the legs — not to pull back necessarily, but to distinguish between productive load and early overreach.
